intent: Deliver the two remaining pieces: an in-app way to set the home coordinates (run-as is dead on the release build device owner requires), and DISALLOW_CONFIG_VPN so the always-on VPN cannot be switched off from Settings.
scope: Non-goal: RethinkDNS blocklist selection, which is user configuration
changes: EnforcementRunner.setHomeToCurrentLocation writes home_location.json from the app's own uid. push_home_location.sh cannot: it stages through `run-as`, which returns 'package not debuggable' on a release build, and making the build debuggable would let anyone with adb edit this app's state -- the bypass the design exists to close.
Deliberately not an exported intent or receiver. Anything that can set home from outside can set it elsewhere, and the geofence would then report AWAY forever with enforcement off.
Coordinates are never logged: that is the user's home address and logcat is readable by anyone with adb.
setVpnConfigBlocked wired through to a UI button with a confirmation dialog, applied only after the filter was confirmed working.
The status page gained a Geofence row. 'no home set - enforcing everywhere' is a large behavioural difference from a working geofence and was previously invisible.
Scaffold body became a SingleChildScrollView: the two new buttons overflowed by 4px, and an unreachable 'Release device owner' button is the one control that must never be clipped.

verification.evidence: 69 Dart tests (2 new, covering both geofence states), 16 Kotlin tests, analyze clean. The overflow was caught by the widget tests failing with 'A RenderFlex overflowed by 4.0 pixels', i.e. a real UI bug that would have clipped on device.

verification.command: tap 'Set home to current location' on device
verification.evidence: Returned its designed failure: 'no location fix available - open a maps app, then retry'. The write path executes and reports rather than silently no-opping. It cannot complete yet because the wiped phone has no GPS fix (location_mode was 0; set to 3, but last location=null on every provider).
logcat 'DISALLOW_CONFIG_VPN=true'; dumpsys user reports 'Device policy restrictions: no_config_vpn'. `settings put secure always_on_vpn_app ""` afterwards did not unpin it.

verification.command: does DISALLOW_CONFIG_VPN lock RethinkDNS's own settings? (the open question)
verification.evidence: No. Navigated RethinkDNS's UI under the restriction and changed its blocklist selection successfully (188 -> 170 -> 169 lists). The restriction governs system VPN configuration, not the VPN app's internal settings.

verification.command: reboot, then re-verify the whole stack
verification.evidence: Device Owner Type: 0, mAlwaysOnVpnPackage=com.celzero.bravedns, no_config_vpn still enforced, youtube hidden=true, uninstall still DELETE_FAILED_DEVICE_POLICY_MANAGER, youtube.com still 127.0.0.1.

verification.command: final DNS state after the user disabled the 'no google' blocklist
verification.evidence: All 14 YouTube domains BLOCKED (127.0.0.1). google.com, accounts.google.com, play.google.com, mail.google.com, googleapis.com, gstatic.com all resolve to real IPs. Controls wikipedia.org, github.com, cloudflare.com, kernel.org resolve normally.

risks: The geofence is still not active: no home_location.json, so every pass decides LOCATION_UNKNOWN and enforcement applies everywhere. One tap of the new button at home fixes it, once the phone has a GPS fix.
The AWAY branch remains unit-tested only. It cannot be exercised on device until coordinates exist, so the always-blocked exemption has never been observed on real hardware.

A blocklist reload briefly breaks all DNS resolution: three control domains returned nothing immediately after the change and resolved normally ~20s later. Transient, but it means a check run straight after a blocklist edit can look like a failure.

Diagnosing the DNS over-blocking cost several wrong turns: I theorised a wildcard custom rule when the cause was a 'no google' blocklist the user had enabled. Navigating RethinkDNS by coordinate also mis-tapped into Firefox once. Blocklist selection is user configuration and is not visible from adb.
rollback: In-app 'Release device owner' clears DISALLOW_CONFIG_VPN, unpins the VPN and unblocks uninstall before releasing -- verified end to end on this device while the account count was still 0.
To lift only the VPN lock, call setVpnConfigBlocked(false); the method takes a boolean and the UI button currently only sets it true.
